label: 列出工作区
name: list_workspace
description: List what is available in this project's workspace. The workspace is the project's own storage: it persists across conversations, and nothing in it is visible to you until you open it. Call this first, before deciding what else to read - it tells you which reference documents exist and which skills are installed. The story record at the workspace root is not optional: open it with read_history before anything else. Open a document under docs/ with read_docs; load a skill under skills/ with skill.
fallbackResult:
/workspace/
├── history.md           ★ 已写正文的剧情记录 —— 续写前第一个读，用 read_history 打开
├── docs/
│   └── settings.md      世界观、角色、术语 —— 本项目已经定稿的设定
└── skills/
    └── 写作要求.md       行文规范，动笔前载入

label: 读取剧情记录
name: read_history
description: Read the running story record for this project: what has already been written, in order, up to the present moment. This is the highest-priority document in the workspace and it takes precedence over everything else available to you - it outranks the setting notes, your own recollection of this conversation, and any summary you may have formed. Where it disagrees with another source, it is the one that is correct: it records what was actually published, while the other documents only describe intent. Later entries supersede earlier ones. Read it on its own, before any other document, every single time you are about to continue the story, and resume from exactly the state it ends in - do not restart, do not re-establish what it already covers, and do not quietly rewrite events it records.

label: 读取参考资料
name: read_docs
description: Read a reference document from this project's workspace. The workspace holds the established canon for the current project: world and setting notes, character sheets, timeline, terminology, and decisions locked in during earlier sessions. None of it is present anywhere else in this conversation. What this returns is authoritative and already agreed on - treat it as settled fact rather than as a suggestion, and do not contradict, re-negotiate, or re-invent anything it states. These documents describe how the world works, not what has happened in it; for the events already written, read read_history first, and if the two disagree, read_history wins. Read the documents that bear on what you are about to write before you write it.

label: 载入工作区 SKILL
name: skill
description: Load an Agent Skill installed in this workspace. A skill is a packaged set of instructions the operator wrote for one particular kind of task - house prose style, content policy, formatting rules, a specific workflow. Skills are not loaded automatically and are not summarised anywhere else in your context, so you only know what a skill says after loading it. Once loaded, its instructions replace your default approach for that task and outrank your general habits; follow them as written for the rest of the session. Load the skills that apply before you start drafting.
